help.title: Help
help.welcomeDesc: This tool helps check the accuracy of citations in academic papers, verifying whether cited references exist and match the details you wrote.
help.decisionSupportDesc: This system provides analysis to assist expert review. Final judgment on citation integrity requires human expertise.
help.step1: Upload your document (PDF, Word .docx, or reference files .bib, .ris)
help.step2: Extracts your citations automatically (including scanned PDFs and older Vietnamese fonts)
help.step3: Checks each citation across 15+ international academic libraries, official registries, and live or archived web pages
help.step4: View detailed results and your Citation Integrity Score (CIS)
help.step5: Export your report as PDF, Word (.docx), CSV, or JSON
help.gs1Desc: Go to New Check and drag & drop your PDF (.pdf), Word (.docx), or reference file — BibTeX (.bib) or RIS (.ris) (5MB–100MB depending on plan; automatically reads scanned PDFs and older Vietnamese fonts).
help.gs2Desc: Checking typically takes 30–60 seconds depending on document length. You can watch live progress.
help.gs3Desc: View your Citation Integrity Score (CIS) and examine individual citation results. Click any citation for detailed information.
help.gs4Desc: Download your verification report as PDF, Word (.docx), CSV, or JSON to save or share with your instructor.
help.cisDesc: The Citation Integrity Score (CIS) is a 0–100 summary of your citations' accuracy: 85–100 Excellent, 70–84 Good, 50–69 Needs Review, and below 50 Needs Careful Review.
help.shortcutsIntro: Use these shortcuts for faster navigation:

sharedReport.qrSealSubtitle: Tamper-protected verification link for this report
sharedReport.noVerdicts: No citation results recorded for this document.
sharedReport.disclaimer: This system is a decision-support tool designed to assist instructors and researchers in reviewing citation integrity in academic documents. Two-step verification (matching in-text citations to reference entries and verifying source existence) provides evidence-based suggestions from public academic libraries (Crossref, OpenAlex, DBLP, arXiv, Europe PMC, DataCite) with transparent explanations. A "Source Not Found" label is a review flag only — it does not prove a source is fabricated. The instructor or human reviewer makes the final decision. This system does not conclude academic misconduct, does not fact-check individual manuscript claims, and does not penalize citing the same valid source multiple times.
